title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 24
paragraphs: With these words Megabazus easily persuaded Darius, who took him for a true prophet of what was likely to come to pass. Thereupon Darius sent a messenger to Myrcinus with this message: “Histiaeus, King Darius says this: Reflecting, I find that there is no one more sincerely well-disposed than you to me and my power; and this I know by deeds, not words. Now therefore, since I have it in mind to accomplish great matters, by all means come here to me, so that I may share them with you.” Trusting these words, and at the same time counting it a great thing to become a counselor of the king, Histiaeus came to Sardis; and when he had come, Darius spoke to him as follows: “Histiaeus, I sent for you for this reason: that when I had returned from the Scythians and you had gone out of my sight, never did I desire to see anything again so quickly as I then wished both to see you and to come to speech with you—since I perceived that the most valuable of all possessions is a friend who is a man of understanding and also sincerely well-disposed, both of which qualities I know exist in you, and of which I can bear witness in my own affairs. Now then—since you have done well to come here—this is what I propose to you: leave Miletus alone and your newly founded city in Thrace, and come with me to Susa; share whatever I have, eat at my table, and be my counselor.”
